title.title: Gersten's conjecture fails for ramified regular local rings
title.subtitle: Claim: explicit regular local rings $A$ of mixed characteristic $(0,5)$ where $K_3(A) \to K_3(\mathrm{Frac}\,A)$ has a kernel

plain: A rule that a ring's K-theory never loses information when you allow fractions fails for some rings

lines.tex: A = \text{its local ring at a point of the special fibre},\ \ \pi \in \mathfrak m^2

beats.text: One explicit hypersurface, in mixed characteristic $(0,5)$
Its local ring is regular, two-dimensional and ramified
A $K_3$ class (and a $K_5$ class) dies over the fraction field: injectivity fails

achievement.label: Gersten's conjecture (1973)
achievement.context: Before: true when $A$ contains a field (Quillen, Panin) and for rings smooth over a DVR (Gillet–Levine)
achievement.note: Ramified rings, integral coefficients only; the unramified case is untouched

verify.ourCheck: We read the claim and the review; we did not check the proof

voice.text: Gersten's conjecture fails for ramified rings.
Gersten: a regular local ring's K-theory injects into its fraction field's.
It was known whenever the ring contains a field.
Claimed: explicit ramified rings where a K three class dies.

sources.quote: (local rings of explicit hypersurfaces such as (X−Z)^5 − XY^4 + Y^5 + ζZ^5 = 0 at a point of the special fibre, with π ∈ m²) such that K_3(A) → K_3(Frac A) and K_5(A) → K_5(Frac A) have nonzero kernel
explicit two-dimensional ramified regular local rings A of mixed characteristic (0,5)
Gersten (1973 problem); Quillen (1973) proved it for regular local rings essentially of finite type over a field; Panin (2003) full equicharacteristic; Gillet–Levine (1987) smooth over a DVR
Ramified only (π ∈ m²) and integral coefficients; the unramified mixed-characteristic case and finite-coefficient forms are untouched.
